## Why H33 could have improved — and what cannot be concluded

The local forensic record (`evidence/h33_forensics_20261024.json`) identifies nested ridge-support thinning and catalogue-collar removal in the H33 family. For the shared evaluator,

`DTI = T / (T + 0.2 FP + 0.8 FN)`.

Removing a redundant prediction that adds FP but no truth coverage can improve this ratio. Kernel-aware thinning can remove redundant support; catalogue masking can make near-known-fault predictions unproductive. These are **conditional metric mechanisms**, not proof of causation on hidden labels. Removing a point that provides unique coverage can instead harm DTI.

The values **0.2778**, **0.3195**, and **0.4413** in the request are **USER-REPORTED CLAIMS**, not ORGANIZER-CONFIRMED measurements in this session. A public page repeating a claim is not a submission receipt. The current official leaderboard, weekly allowance, rules PDF, and hidden labels were not retrieved here. No projection or implied hidden-label count is a score. Nothing in the audited local evidence proves a new file will exceed any of those claims.

Stored MDPS-88 **HOLDOUT-DTI**, evaluator `gems57-pooled-hide-v2`:

| Endpoint | Candidate; 95% CI | Withheld positive pixels | Interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Overall | 0.066728; [0.055112, 0.078420] | 22,893 | Below paired control point estimate 0.108541; control 95% CI [0.094883, 0.121052]. |
| Far | 0.072723; [0.059113, 0.086283] | 10,791 | Paired HOLDOUT-DTI difference vs control +0.003596, 95% CI [-0.006021, 0.012788]; does not establish improvement. |

These are inherited hide-and-recover results, not newly trained results. `validate_mdps88.py` independently recomputes their pooled arithmetic from saved fold terms; this does not reproduce training, feature provenance, or confidence intervals. The single-feature canary is inherited evidence (44 features; max symmetric AUC 0.594755), not a new canary run. Known-fault holdout recovery need not generalize to new off-catalogue faults.

## Ranked research backlog — NOT implemented or promoted

Novelty is scoped to the reviewed local modules, not every experiment on all listed sites. Existing code already includes gravity/magnetic edges, cross-gradients, magnetic residuals, radiometric contrasts, pluvial penalties, geodesic relays, and distance-regime allocation. Proposing those generic ideas again is not novelty. The following are distinct **extensions requiring a fresh novelty review and preregistration**, not established discoveries. Expected benefit is a qualitative research priority, never predicted DTI.

| Rank | Proposed exact layers and transform | Missing-fault rationale; named non-fault mimic | Difference from reviewed code; cost and uncertainty |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Existing DEM + LiDAR-scarp context: follow candidate contour-parallel scarps, fit constant-elevation vs fault-like variable-elevation models, use held-out along-trace residual likelihood ratio as a veto. | Could remove Lahontan shoreline benches while retaining previously unmapped scarps that cut across elevation contours. **Mimic:** fluvial terrace risers. Flat or contour-parallel real faults could be wrongly removed. | Existing pluvial penalties are local indices; this proposes trace-level competing geomorphic model fits with out-of-trace prediction. Potential: moderate precision gain; cost: medium. |
| 2 | Existing magnetic and gravity grids: cross-wavelet phase congruency with local phase agreement across scales, conditioned on depth-to-basement. | Buried density/susceptibility discontinuities could persist across scales despite weak surface relief. **Mimic:** unfaulted intrusive contacts. | Not PHASE-88 cross-gradient disagreement or scalar residual maxima; joint cross-scale phase stability is the proposed new feature. Potential: uncertain moderate; cost: medium/high. |
| 3 | Existing elevation/chi context: matched catchment pairs on opposite sides of candidate lineaments, test stream-profile knickpoint residual alignment after conditioning on drainage area and relief. | Correlated displaced stream profiles could reveal subtle unmapped deformation. **Mimic:** migrating base-level knickpoints at lithologic boundaries. | Existing chi/ridge columns are pointwise; paired catchment counterfactual matching is different. Potential: uncertain; cost: high; raster resolution may be inadequate. |
| 4 | Existing magnetic grid: local 2-D spectral comb score and spatial phase stability as an acquisition-artifact veto, cross-checked against gravity rather than treated as positive fault evidence. | Might reduce flight-parallel false positives and free prediction mass for off-catalogue support. **Mimic:** real parallel volcanic dikes. | Existing seam indicators are present; the extension is an explicit periodic-comb null model with held-out window validation. Potential: low/uncertain; cost: medium. |

No new external dataset is needed conceptually for these proposals. **Availability is not overstated:** only sample/catalogue/registry mirrors were restored in this session; full features and external cached derivatives were not restored. Existing stack provenance and per-layer coverage must be checked before declaring a hypothesis executable. For new external flight paths or higher-resolution terrain, the official sources below are leads only; AOI files, licenses and obtainability are unverified in this network and thus not viable inputs yet.

Top candidate testing is **blocked**, not silently skipped: the pre-placement saturation certificate already forces duplicate-stop. After an explicitly approved shared protocol resolves the contradiction, first verify novelty/inputs; then freeze whole-component buffered folds, derive all catalogue features from visible faults only, run each feature's leakage canary, compare paired pooled DTI and spatial-block CI against the same-fold incumbent, and stop within the experiment budget. Reuse the existing evaluator/writer. Never score an H33 fixed raster on folds as a fold-fair trained baseline.
